correctness.rationale: With M=n+t+1, the full word set partitions into equal parts of size q^(t+1) by literal prefix. At each r≥1 a word has at most B_r=M−r+1 descendants; a descendant has at most B_r q^r preimages by block reinsertion, including the starting word. Thus the degree of the union over 1≤r≤t is at most the sum of B_r(B_r q^r−1), which is at most M²(q^(t+1)−q)/(q−1) and strictly less than q^(t+1)/2 when q>2M²+1. The hypotheses of the independent-transversal criterion hold, so one representative per prefix suffices; r=0 uses distinct codewords and different r give different output lengths. The least power of two above 2M²+1 is strictly below twice that odd integer. The proof covers trailer deletions since positions are counted in the full transmitted word.
residual_risks: No exhaustive enumeration is needed. The transversal proves joint existence, not a pointwise efficient encoder or optimal alphabet size.

evidence: Theorem 2.5 corrects up to k arbitrary deletions with k+1 symbols at q≥2 binom(M,k)². This is broader error coverage, but grows as M^(2k) for fixed k≥2; k=1 is already quadratic. Theorem 7.1 treats adjacent bursts of up to two with n+3 total length and a polynomial-time construction with quartic alphabet bound. Its Theorem 8.1 shows three redundant symbols necessary for n≥2 in that setting.

Wang et al. give an even-q code at bit redundancy log n+O(log q log log n); Ye–Ge give log n+O_(q,t)(1) at fixed q,t. Neither cited statement supplies the growing-q literal-systematic trailer guarantee.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General deletion correction is not a dominating bound when its alphabet hypothesis is stronger. Efficient encoding and smaller alphabet are distinct resources here; the t=1 case carries no claimed order improvement.

evidence: Equation (1) has the same single-radius degree-counting pattern B(Bq^k−1), with B=binom(M,k). Theorem 2.5 uses exact-k arbitrary-deletion correction and invokes a separate lemma to cover shorter arbitrary deletions. Haxell's theorem supplies a transversal only once the conflict degree has been bounded.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior proofs suggest the method directly. The stated hypotheses of Theorem 2.5, however, do not furnish the quadratic bound; it requires the contiguous position count and a union across all allowed lengths. No new transversal theorem is claimed.

evidence: A systematic prefix representative is equivalent here to an independent transversal of prefix parts in the full-word conflict graph. The preceding independent-transversal benchmark uses this exact partition but counts arbitrary k-position sets.
Nonbinary burst codes correct the same channel, but a redundancy bound for unrestricted words does not give one representative for every literal prefix.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Relabeling trailers as redundant symbols or modeling a burst by a contiguous reinsertion does not convert an unrestricted code or a quartic-alphabet t=2 construction into this quadratic-alphabet guarantee.

originality.rationale: The prefix-transversal framework and the one-length insertion/descendant counting argument are directly antecedent. The supported distinct guarantee is simultaneous correction of all contiguous lengths through t with exactly t+1 deletion-prone appended symbols at quadratic alphabet size, independent of t in the exponent. None of the closest inspected claims dominates the full resource and correction regime.
residual_risks: Priority is bounded by inspected literature and catalogue matches; a prior pattern-family bound with the same quantitative resources could change the assessment.

value.rationale: Deletion-prone systematic redundancy is the substantive constraint. Through t=2 the result attains the necessary three trailer symbols with a quadratic rather than quartic alphabet-size guarantee, at the stated cost of losing efficient encoding. For arbitrary t it keeps the exponent fixed while retaining the t+1-symbol trailer. This is a meaningful resource-regime gain over the inspected existence benchmark, despite the short degree estimate and standard transversal step.
residual_risks: No uniform algorithm, pointwise efficient construction, or matching alphabet lower bound is claimed; bit-redundancy optima for unrestricted codes do not follow.
